designSummary: Descriptive implementation study; proportions with confidence intervals by home and in total, and monthly run charts of adoption and recommendations carried out.
sampleSize: All residents are included, so there is no sampling. With about 168 residents in the first six months, a reach of 70 percent is estimated with a 95 percent confidence interval of about plus or minus 7 percentage points overall and about plus or minus 11 points in the largest home (64 beds). Falls are expected at about 5 per 1,000 resident-days, about 300 falls a year across the homes, which describes the rate but cannot show a small change.
primaryAnalysis: Reach as a proportion with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, overall and by home, against the pre-stated target of 70 percent.
secondaryAnalysis: Rounds held per home (target 10 of 12); recommendations carried out within four weeks; checklist completion index; change in regular medicines per resident from baseline to 12 months as a mean difference with its interval; falls per 1,000 resident-days and restarts within 30 days, described monthly.
missingData: Residents who die or leave before six months contribute to reach only while resident; missing round notes are counted as rounds not documented, not imputed.
multiplicity: One primary outcome with a target; other measures are descriptive.
software: Spreadsheet templates for monthly counts, with R for intervals; export and linkage rules archived before January.
overfittingGuards: Targets and outcome definitions fixed before the first round
No home-level comparisons presented as effects
Falls described, never tested for benefit
summary: Whole-population measurement; reach of 70 percent estimated within about 7 points; clinical measures descriptive.
